title: Tauri v2 capabilities and permissions security
keyFindings: Tauri v2 combines command permissions, resource or parameter scopes, and window or webview capabilities.
IPC authorization considers the command, window, webview, and local or remote origin before invocation.
Remote content cannot reach custom commands without an explicit remote capability.
Command implementations remain responsible for interpreting and enforcing attached scopes.
Filesystem, HTTP, shell, and sidecar authority can be narrowed, while CSP provides complementary frontend defense.
Tauri ACL is not an OS sandbox or a replacement for application authorization and workload isolation.
prepSchoolImplications: Separate capability roles by exact window and webview labels.
Keep privileged webviews local and avoid remote capabilities by default.
Expose typed semantic lab commands instead of arbitrary host primitives.
Enforce authentication, session policy, interview integrity, and resource isolation in trusted shared logic and the local-lab agent.
Use per-session filesystem and network scopes, exact sidecars, restrictive CSP, and explicit recording consent.
Test both capability manifests and native out-of-scope rejection in CI.
openQuestions: Whether PrepSchool should adopt Tauri at all.
What minimum typed command surface the desktop client needs.
What local transport and per-session authentication model the agent should use.
What OS-level sandboxing is required on each supported platform.
How to prevent symlink and parent-directory escapes in user-selected path scopes.
Which plugin default permissions, if any, are acceptable.
How capability drift will be detected during upgrades.
